ALF TAYLOR. A regular member of our cross country teams of the thirties which figured so prominently in the Southern and National Championships.

It was in 1931 that Ken O'Kell signed up Alf Taylor and Bert Mitchell, after beating the former in a 1 mile race at AEC Southall. After moving to Ford's Dagenham in 1932, Ken discovered that both lads were also Ford workers.

He was not one of the stars who featured in our formidable teams of the '30s and '40s, but he was a sound supporting runner who frequently featured in 12-to-score teams and on one occasion was just pipped for sixth scorer by Alf Taylor when the ``Southern'' was held at Taplow.
